characters.name: In General
characters.description: Alliterative Family: Three out of the four family members have a name beginning with "B": Bluey, Bingo, and Bandit, with Chilli beingthe only exception. Energetic and Soft-Spoken Duo: Although it’s downplayed since they can both be very energetic during games, Bluey is considerably more loud and talkative compared to Bingo, who’s more soft-spoken and shy. Foolish Sibling, Responsible Sibling: As revealed in "Mini Bluey", Bluey is rather messy and isn't very willing to help with house chores, while Bingo is neater and is more willing to help out. Four-Temperament Ensemble:Bluey is an imaginativeGenki Girl(Sanguine).Bingo is shyer and more responsible than Bluey, as well asWise Beyond Her Years(Melancholic).Bandit is aReformed Bullyto his brother and occasionally goes too far when playing with his daughters without realizing (Choleric).Chilli is a levelheadedDeadpan Snarker(Phlegmatic). Bluey is an imaginativeGenki Girl(Sanguine).

characters.name: Bluey
characters.description: Aesop Amnesia:Bluey often learns that she shouldn't ignore Bingo's feelings, or disregard her input during their games, but ends up forgetting this lesson in short order.Justified, considering Bluey is only six years old.In "Show and Tell", Bluey openly admits that she completely forgot the lesson she learned in "Tina". Bluey often learns that she shouldn't ignore Bingo's feelings, or disregard her input during their games, but ends up forgetting this lesson in short order.Justified, considering Bluey is only six years old. In "Show and Tell", Bluey openly admits that she completely forgot the lesson she learned in "Tina". Ancestral Name: Her middle name, Christine, is taken from Bandit's mother's first name. Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!: Could be chalked up to her age, but in multiple episodes Bluey has difficulty focusing and remembering what she's doing, particularly in the episode "Hide and Seek". She is also seen using a stim toy in "Magic".

characters.name: Bingo
characters.description: Big Sister Instinct: Inverted. Bingo (who's ironically more sensitive) has been shown to be protective of her older sister, Bluey. Twice.In "The Dump", Bandit throws away some of Bluey's drawings and this makes Bluey cry. Bingo call Bandit a "Baddie" for this. Bingo then goes back in the car to console Bluey.In "The Sign", she yells and barks at the people taking Bluey's bed. In "The Dump", Bandit throws away some of Bluey's drawings and this makes Bluey cry. Bingo call Bandit a "Baddie" for this. Bingo then goes back in the car to console Bluey. In "The Sign", she yells and barks at the people taking Bluey's bed. Break the Cutie: Due to her emotional nature, Bingo's feelings tend to get hurt quite a lot, often unintentionally. Luckily, she usually gets over it by the end of each episode. Catchphrase:"This is outrageous!"She often lets out an exuberant "Yahhhh!" when she charges into something.And she says "Real!" when she's excited.

characters.name: Bandit (Dad)
characters.description: Bandit is Bluey and Bingo's father, a Blue Heeler who works as a freelance archaeologist. When he's not too busy and/or tired, he enjoys making up games and playing with his daughters. Actor Allusion: As revealed in the minisode “Browny Bear”, Bandit's middle name is "Custard". DavidMcCormack, his voice actor, is the frontman ofa band of the same name. In addition, Bandit's birth date is listed as 25 October 1978, which is exactly ten years afterMcCormack'sown birthday. Affectionate Nickname:Chilli sometimes calls him "Babe".Bluey calls him "Big Daddy" on occasion.Nana calls him "Bandy" in "Christmas Swim". Chilli sometimes calls him "Babe". Bluey calls him "Big Daddy" on occasion.

characters.name: Chilli (Mum)
characters.description: Chilli is Bluey and Bingo's mother, a Red Heeler who works in airport security and juggles this with raising her two little pups. Chilli is often seen commenting wryly on things, consoling unhappy children, joining in on her family's games, and laughing at comical situations. Acquired Situational Narcissism: As she recalls in "Baby Race", she became overly proud of her parenting skills after baby Bluey learned to roll over much earlier than she was meant to. Alliterative Name: Before she got married, her maiden name was Chilli Cattle. Catchphrase: "Wackadoo!"It was phased out after season one(save forBluey: The Videogameas aCall-Back). Country Mouse: "Granddad" reveals that she grew up out in the countryside.

characters.name: Uncle Stripe
characters.description: Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: In his youth, he wore an athlete's headband. Badly Battered Babysitter: Like his brother, he tends to struggle with looking after both his kids, and his nieces. It doesn't help that his daughter Muffin is particularly hard to handle sometimes. Beta Couple: With Trixie, they form a secondary couple to the main couple of Bandit and Chilli. The Dog Bites Back: In the flashback shown in "Fairytale". After being picked on by Bandit all through their holiday, he took great delight in taunting his older brother over being jinxed. Doting Parent: It's indicated at several points that Stripe tends to spoil Muffin, most notably giving her a large power wheel car in "Pizza Girls" and telling her that she's "the most special kid in the world" in "Library".This is often deconstructedthough, as it's implied that Stripe's doting on Muffin fuels herbrattytendencies, with Stripe often reaping what he sows.

characters.name: Aunt Trixie
characters.description: Beta Couple: With Stripe, they form a secondary couple to the main couple of Bandit and Chilli. Big Eater: In "Muffin Cone", she eats an entire bowl of potato chips while Chilli's back is turned. In-Series Nickname: Stripe and Chilli sometimes call her "Trix". Odd Name Out: While "Stripe", "Muffin", and "Socks" are not names people have in real life, "Trixie" is. Passionate Sports Girl: She likes to play hockey with Chilli.

characters.name: Muffin
characters.description: Accidental Bargaining Skills: In "Granny Mobile", Muffin pretends to be a grouchy granny while playing a game with Bluey and Bingo about selling them Doreen's "granny mobile" (i.e. mobility scooter). When an old lady pug comes by and wants to buy it, Muffin, still pretending, argues with her over the price, with Muffin constantly upping it as they argue longer. Due to only being four years old, Muffin just thinks she's playing a game, but in the end she manages to sell the granny mobile for $1200, four times more than Doreen had originally listed for it and twelve times more than Doreen was going to settle for. Acquired Situational Narcissism: In "Library". Being called "the most special kid in the world" by her father leads her to believe she doesn't need to follow the rules of Bluey and Bingo's game, and can do whatever she wants. Affectionate Nickname: Stripe calls her "Muffy" in "Library", and Trixie calls her "Muffles" in "Muffin Cone". All Girls Like Ponies: In "The Quiet Game", she is mentioned to own a collection of Moonlight Unicorn toys and gets angry if she's gifted one that she already has. Annoying Younger Sibling: Downplayed. She usually gets along well with her cousins, but her bratty attitude sometimes leads her to play this role for Bluey and Bingo, as seen in the episode "Charades" and "Library". She's also Bluey and Bingo's younger cousin rather than sister, and Socks'soldersister.

characters.name: Socks
characters.description: Socks is Stripe and Trixie's youngest daughter, a one (later two)-year-old Blue Heeler. Affectionate Nickname: Stripe calls her "Rock-Socks" in "Horsey Ride" and the short "Honk". Anthropomorphic Shift: In the first season, Socks acts like a real puppy would, moving on all fours and generally barking or growling instead of speaking. From "Christmas Swim" onwards, she walks upright on two legs like the rest of the cast and starts speaking more often, while most of her puppy-like habits have disappeared. Artifact Name: Socks' name comes from the fact that her feet used to have a pattern of stripes that make her feet look like socks. However, once she turns two years old, she no longer has them. The Baby of the Bunch: At two years old, she is currently the youngest Heeler family member.

characters.name: Nana Chris
characters.description: '80s Hair: She had a perm back in the 1980s, as shown in "Fairytale" during Bandit's flashbacks to his childhood. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: She wears glasses. Accidental Misnaming: In "Christmas Swim", she calls Bluey's new toy Bartleby, "Bartleboy" and "Bumblebee". Cool Old Lady: In "Grannies", she manages to learn the flossing dance with only a little direction from Bluey. Deliberate Values Dissonance:"Baby Race" shows that Chris' plan to get baby Bluey to walk was to put olive oil on her knees, preventing her from crawling, to Bandit and Chilli's horror.Bandit:This isn't legal anymore!In "Fairytale", she tries to hit Bandit with a sandal, with him commenting that back in the '80s, "mums were allowed to be mean".

characters.name: Grandpa Bob
characters.description: Affectionate Nickname: His wife and grandkids sometimes call him "Bobba". Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Outside of appearing in a family photo in his wife's home and a flashback sequence in "Fairytale", Bob hadn't been seen since his debut in "Grannies", despite his wife appearing without him many times; while many fans took this as evidence of his death,Joe Brumminsisted he was still alive and wouldeventually reappear:he finally turns up in "The Sign" during Rad and Frisky's wedding, where it's revealed that he wason a solo trip in India to "find himself". Ear Notch: He is missing much of the top of his left ear; his appearance in "Fairytale" shows his ear being whole back when Bandit was ten. Humanlike Animal Aging: A possible case: he has a few red spots, which may indicate that his coat may simply havegonegray with age (as human hair does) rather than being naturally that way (and might help explain Rad's coloration). That said, he is also shown to be gray as a middle-aged man in "Fairytale". Took a Level in Kindness: It’s implied in “Fairytale” that he used to be harsher with his sons when they were younger, refusing to lift Bandit’s jinx to keep him quiet and jokingly wanting to figure out how to use it on his other sons as well. In the minisode “Letter”, Bandit also says he yelled at Rad during footy games. In the present as a grandfather he seems to have mellowed out more.

characters.name: Uncle Rad
characters.description: Amazing Technicolor Wildlife: In comparison to other dogs, his fur is noticeably more vibrant. Big Brother Instinct: A rather odd example that also overlaps withBig Brother Bully. In "Fairy Tale", he jinxes Bandit to stop him from picking on Stripe. Commonality Connection: He and Frisky connect over their mutual adoration of Bluey and Bingo, and the end of "Double Babysitter" shows them discussing the brand of shampoo they both like. Cool Uncle: To Bluey and Bingo. He loves to show them a great time whenever he visits them. Early-Bird Cameo: He first appears in "Featherwand", in a small portrait hanging in the Heelers' home; later in "Charades" and "Escape", he can be seen in a family picture in Nana's home.

characters.name: Aunt Frisky
characters.description: Commonality Connection: She and Rad connect over their mutual adoration of Bluey and Bingo, and the end of 'Double Babysitter' shows them discussing the brand of shampoo they both like. Ears as Hair: Implied, as her ears are nowhere to be seen and her "hair" is the same color as her fur. Former Teen Rebel: Implied from Chilli in “The Sign", when she claims she and Frisky used to come to the lookout as teenagers to“um, think”. Friend to All Children: Bluey adores Frisky as her godmother (or "fairy godmother" as she likes to call her) and it's shown in "Double Babysitter" and "The Sign" that she loves kids and gets along great with them. When asked if she wanted children in "Double Babysitter", she replied yes without hesitation. Honorary Aunt: Despite being Bluey's godmother, the credits for 'Double Babysitter' refer to her as "Aunt Frisky", and the Heelers definitely treat her like a member of the family."Christmas Swim" implies that she and Rad have gotten engaged, which would make her a soon to beactualaunt to Bluey and Bingo. The two are officially married in "The Sign", meaning that the "honorary" part has officially been dropped.

characters.name: Grandad Mort
characters.description: Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: He wears a hat. Cool Old Guy: As shown in "Grandad", he loves running around and having fun with Bluey and Bingo, despite having recently had heartworm. Early-Bird Cameo: A picture of him when he was younger was seen hanging on a wall in the Heeler household since the first season. My God, What Have I Done?: When he realises how much his playing around has worried Chilli, he decides to slow down and relax with her. Signature Headgear: His green bucket hat, which he's rarely seen without.

characters.name: Aunty Brandy
characters.description: Aloof Big Sister: Zigzagged. She's Chilli's older sister who hasn't visited the Heeler family for several years; it's heavily implied that she's mainly kept her distance from Chilli becauseshe can't have children and seeing her sister with children of her own is too painful for her. Bluey's Big Play also implies that she and Chillihad an argument that led to a rift that went unresolved for years. However, the play ends with Chilli reaching out to Brandy via a phone call.After that, in "Onesies" she makes an effort to reconnect with Chilli's family and later apologizes to Chilli for staying away for so long, and towards the end it's shown that they're still capable of having fun together. Early-Bird Cameo: She had two:She was first seen as a child in a photo of Chilli's family during "Obstacle Course".She also factors intoBluey's Big Play, the travelling stage show with life-size puppets. Chillimentions that sometimes, sisters start arguing and forget to stop.At the end of the play, her voice appears when Chilligets the courage to reach out and calls her. She was first seen as a child in a photo of Chilli's family during "Obstacle Course". She also factors intoBluey's Big Play, the travelling stage show with life-size puppets. Chillimentions that sometimes, sisters start arguing and forget to stop.At the end of the play, her voice appears when Chilligets the courage to reach out and calls her. Earn Your Happy Ending:After years of struggling with what's implied to have been fertility problems, "The Sign" shows that she's visibly pregnant with her long desired child.

characters.name: Chilli's Mum
characters.description: Good Parents: From the little we saw of her in "Dragon", she was a supportive mother, encouraging a younger Chilli to keep drawing horses. No Name Given: She's only referred to as "Chilli's Mum" (in the credits of "Dragon") and "Mrs. Cattle" (in the official family tree). Posthumous Character: She's dead in the present time. The way Bluey talks about her from Chilli's flashback implies she died either when Bluey was very young or before Bluey was born.

characters.name: Pat
characters.description: A Golden Labrador Retriever who is Lucky's father, and a neighbour to the Heelers. Butt-Monkey: He often ends up getting caught in the crossfire of the Heeler family's games. Catchphrase: "Aw yeah, righto!" whenever he needs to leap into action. Country Mouse: "Dad Baby" reveals that he grew up on a sorghum farm. A Day in the Limelight: He's the main focus of "Pass the Parcel", which revolves around his efforts to see the titular game played the "right" way.

characters.name: Janelle
characters.description: A Labrador retriever and Pat's wife, Lucky and Chucky's mum, a neighbour to the Heelers as well. Happily Married: Despite the sports team divide, she's cheerfully married to Pat. Opposing Sports Team: Roots for the "blue" teamnotethe New South Wales BluesinRugby Leaguewhile Pat and Lucky both root for "purple".notethe Queensland MaroonsThis causes friction for Chucky, who thinks that the team preference is driving a wedge between the two. Shared Family Quirks: Like her husband, she and Lucky both watch sports on TV. Unseen No More: For most of the first two seasons, she was never shown onscreen, with her husband often calling for her. She finally makes her first appearance in "Pass the Parcel".

characters.name: Lucky
characters.description: Obsessive Sports Fan: A big fan ofRugby Leaguelike his dad, and cheers for the same team as he does. Odd Name Out: He is the only member of his family not to have a real-life name. Out of Focus: Lucky arguably has the least amount of focus of all the recurring characters. His apparencies are very sporadic and the few times he does appear he is a background character or gets sidelined in favor of the rest of his family. Even his mum Janelle and his younger brother Chucky have arguably gotten more focus than him despite only appearing in 2 episodes.

characters.name: Chucky
characters.description: The Baby of the Bunch: The youngest of the Heeler family's immediate neighbours. A Day in the Limelight: He is the focus of "The Decider" with his difficulty and insecurity in choosing between his parents (even if only over which sports team to root for) being the emotional crux of the story. Obsessive Sports Fan: The only member of his family to avert the trope, as a big part of "The Decider" is him deciding which team he wants to root for between the one his dad cheers fornotethe Queensland MaroonsRugby Leagueteamand the one his mom cheers fornotethe New South Wales Blues, purely based on how sad they look when their teams are losing. By the end, though, he manages to find a common ground by rooting for the "gold" team,notethe Austalian WallabiesRugby Unionteamwhich his entire family supports.

characters.name: Wendy
characters.description: A Chow Chow from England, another neighbour of the Heelers, and the mother of Judo. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: She wears a silver brooch. She also is seen wearing a yellow headband and wristbands when exercising. Ascended Extra: She's gone from being a minor character whose only role was to be mortified by the Heelers' antics to a supporting character with some focus of her own, as well as serving as the agent of Bandit's comeuppance on several occasions. British Stuffiness: She's originally fron England according to the official site, and she tends to be uptight and stuffy. Butt-Monkey: She often finds herself being mortified by the Heelers' antics.

characters.name: Judo
characters.description: A Chow Chow, and Bluey's next-door neighbour. Accents Aren't Hereditary: Judo's mother Wendy is English and speaks with a British accent, but Judo herself doesn't. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: She wears a blue-and-yellow headband. "Baby Race" shows that when she was a baby, she wore a pink hair bow. Always Someone Better: In "Baby Race", Chilli recounts how as a baby Judo reached many developmental steps before Bluey did (sitting upright, crawling, standing, walking). That said, it's downplayed as the crux of the story is Chilli talking about her own doubts as a new mother from seeing Judo learn faster than Bluey makes her wonder if she's a poor mother, until Coco's mom (who had eight kids before Coco) assured her she was doing fine, which made Chilli confident in Bluey's own development. Canine Confusion: She has a red tongue like the other dogs instead of a bluish-black one like a real Chow Chow.

characters.name: Doreen
characters.description: An elderly Great Pyrenees who is a neighbour of the Heeler family. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: She wears hair curlers and glasses. Cool Old Lady: Doreen is very lively and friendly with the Heeler family and seem to be good friends as much as being good neighbours. Extreme Doormat: In "Granny Mobile"; she takes to selling some of her old things to raise the money for a holiday, but is unable to be firm with prospective buyers, instead allowing them to pay whattheythink the items are worth. Grew a Spine: She spends most of "Granny Mobile" being unable to be firm with her buyers, letting them decide prices for the things she's selling, even when they are way too cheap to fund her vacation. She was even willing to sell the titular scooter for only $100 when she had it listed for $300, and even then Bandit thought she should've listed it for more than that. When she witnesses Muffin go toe to toe with the grouchy old lady pug and is able to successfully sell the scooter for $1200 as a result, Doreen shows she's now more confident in herself and is willing to haggle for better deals, seen when she jacks up the price of some exercise equipment she offers to Bandit from his $20 offer to $50.

characters.name: Coco
characters.description: Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: She wears two blue butterfly hair pins. Best Friend: To Indy. When Coco wants to keep playing the titular game in the "Wild Girls" episode instead of playing farmers with everyone else, Indy sticks with her far longer than anyone else and only leaves after having a talk with Coco about Calypso. Even then, she plays with Coco again once she makes a compromise to merge the games. Canine Confusion: She has pink fur, which is not a colour real-life dogs can have. Control Freak: Both "Shadowlands" and "Wild Girls" show that Coco prefers to control the games she plays. Edible Theme Naming: Her name derives fromcoconut.

characters.name: Rusty
characters.description: The Ace: At cricket. Practice makes perfect, so much so that none of the adults trying their hardest can take his wicket. Ambiguously Related: At one point, the official website stated Rusty was one of Bluey's cousins. But for whatever reason, the description was changed to Rusty being one of Bluey's friends instead. Within the series it has never been explicitly said that Bluey and Rusty are related, but the theory is up in the air. Best Friend: To Jack. Rusty was the first friend Jack made at the Glasshouse Primary School and the first dog to help through his physical and mental quirks (implied to be ADHD). Brutal Honesty: In "The Sign"; when Pretzel mentions his pet guinea pig running away, Rusty bluntly suggests that a snake ate him. Cool Big Bro: On the giving and receiving end of this trope. His older brother Digger has no problems with Rusty playing cricket with him and his friends (aside from warning him that they might be a bit rougher than he's used to), and Rusty himself is nothing but loving to his younger sister Dusty.

characters.name: Jack
characters.description: Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!: He has a hard time focusing or sitting still, with the creators confirming that he has ADHD. Fortunately, playing army games with Rusty helps him. Best Friend: To Rusty. Rusty has been shown to get rides home from Jack's parents and has been to his house a lot. Brutal Honesty: In "Helicopter", he bluntly tells Bluey that her idea for a game they're playing is less fun. Elsewhere, he is the first to admit that his ADHD limits him (evenexaggerating those limitationsby accident). A Day in the Limelight:He and Rusty are the primary focus of the episode "Army".He's also the main focus of "Explorers", in which his family gets some focus as well. He and Rusty are the primary focus of the episode "Army".

characters.name: Chloe
characters.description: A Dalmatian who is one of Bluey's classmates, as well as one of her best friends. Best Friend: Her original description labeled her as this to Bluey, though it has since been changed to "one of" them. A Day in the Limelight: She's the most dominant character in "The Adventure" and "Octopus". Informed Attribute: The original description for Chloe stated that she was Bluey's best friend, but it isn't nearly as obvious as Bingo and Lila or Jack and Rusty. While she does appear often among Bluey's lineup of friends, the same can be said for several other characters (Mackenzie, Honey, Coco, etc). The new description refers to her as "one of" Bluey's best friends. Innocently Insensitive: In "Octopus", she hurts her dad's feelings by pointing out he doesn't make the game as fun as Bluey's dad does, yet she had no intention of hurting his feelings; she was just frustrated and didn't realize he'd take it badly.

characters.name: Mackenzie
characters.description: A Border Collie from New Zealand who is one of Bluey's classmates/close friends. A Day in the Limelight: He is the primary focus of the episode "Space", along with Jack and Rusty. The Eeyore: Many of his appearances involve him being uncomfortable or frustrated with the pace other children set during games. He is prone to running off on his own when things don't go his way, and generally comes across as shyer and more sensitive than the other boys. Fast Tunnelling: In "Mums and Dads", he digs multiple holes to the bottom of the kindergarten sandpit. Friendly Rivalry: He often has disagreements with Bluey as seen in "Shops" and "Barky Boats" but they are good friends.

characters.name: Indy
characters.description: An Afghan Hound who is one of Bluey's classmates/close friends. Best Friend: To Coco. Season 3's "Wild Girls" shows that Indy is by far Coco's favorite classmate to play with and she becomes very jealous when Indy wants to play a different game with everyone else. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: Downplayed. Indy has longerears/braidsin the earlier episodes, but they're shorter in her later appearances since her earlier hairstyle made her harder to animate. Her design has largely stayed the same otherwise. Ears as Hair: Her ears are tied off at the ends to look like pigtails; in earlier episodesher ears are much longer and resemble braids, before they were made shorter in order to be easier to animate.Truth in Television, since real Afghan hounds have ears that look a lot like hair. Granola Girl: Her hippie-like clothing and diet (she is not allowed wheat, gluten, sugar, dairy or food with added ingredients) heavily implies that she's being raised as one. Her mother has a very hippie-like fashion sense as well.

characters.name: Honey
characters.description: A mindful Beagle who is one of Bluey's classmates/close friends. Academic Athlete: "Alongside" reveals that she plays sports, and she's described as "mindful" on the official website. Accents Aren't Hereditary: While Honey speaks with an Australian accent, her parents are confirmed to be from the U.K. and have British dialects. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: She wears glasses. Bespectacled Cutie: She's a sweet kid, and she wears green glasses.

characters.name: Snickers
characters.description: An energetic Dachshund who is one of Bluey's classmates/close friends. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: He wears a hat. Edible Theme Naming: His name happens to be the name of a candy bar. Fur Pattern Naming: His body is long and brown like a Snickers bar. Height Angst: Downplayed; it's not so much his height that Snickers has an issue with, it's his long "sausage dog" body that doesn't let him even sit properly at first, which gives him a bit of grief in "Typewriter". He finds a way to enjoy it later, at least.

characters.name: Winton
characters.description: A bulldog who is one of Bluey's classmates. Ascended Extra: Went from having one minor speaking role in Season 1 to being a regular character in Season 2. Class Clown: In "Stories" at least, Winton enjoys playing around and trying to amuse people, which Calypso says is typical behavior for him. Desperately Needs Orders: In "Mums and Dads", Winton is recruited by Indy toplay the eponymous gamewith her. He agrees to take care of the "baby" Polly, while Indy goes to "work"... only to keep pestering her by asking exactly what he's supposed to do in his role. Missing Mom: Implied. We see Winton's dad, but never his mom. In the episode "Helicopter", he says that his mom and dad no longer live together, and the episode "TV Shop" shows that his father has tried to scratch out a decal on his car representing her.

characters.name: The Terriers
characters.description: All There in the Script: Their first names as given byWord of Godare presumably in the scripts, as one of them being named Joe made it into the French dub before being officially revealed, and are used to identify them in the animation files, though those also give them the surname Grumm rather than Terrier. Disappeared Dad: "The Sign" reveals that their dad is not around (it's unknown if he's divorced or dead), with their mother getting together with Winton's father. Everyone Calls Him "Barkeep": So far, the individual brothers have all gone unnamed. Everyone just refers to them collectively as "the Terriers".According to creator Joe Brummin theBehind Blueypodcast, they're named Joe, Dan, and Adam after himself and his two brothers. Last-Name Basis: It'simpliedthat "Terrier" istheir last name. In "Early Baby", one of the only occasions in which one of the three is singled out from the others, Indy addresses Adam as "Terrier"; otherwise, everyone else just refers to them collectively as "the Terriers". Same-Sex Triplets: All three of them are boys and nearly identical to each other save for fur color and height.

characters.name: Pretzel
characters.description: Edible Theme Naming: His name comes from a German pastry. Meaningful Name: His coloration resembles a pretzel, complete with a prominent white spot that looks like a big grain of salt. Out of Focus: He has the least number of appearances and speaking lines out of his other classmates. The Quiet One: He is not as talkative compared to his classmates. Unsuccessful Pet Adoption: In "The Sign", he tells the class about his pet guinea pig running away.

characters.name: Pom Pom
characters.description: The Baby of the Bunch: Of Bingo and Bluey's friends, Pom Pom is the youngest (turning 5 in "Pass the Parcel") and is also the shortest. Character Development: "Seesaw" has Pom Pom initially self-conscious over her small height but by the end she learns that she can still do great things even while small. A Day in the Limelight: "Seesaw", her debut episode no less. The episode focuses on herHeight Angstand coming to embrace her small stature. Fur Pattern Naming: Her name is a reference to her fluffy fur. Furry Reminder: Her being small is a reference to real-life Pomeranians, and she climbs up the seesaw on all fours.

characters.name: Missy
characters.description: Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: She wears decorations in her fur. Character Development: She gets over her fear of the fast-rocking hammock in "Pirates" by climbing into the "whale's mouth" to save her friends. Cowardly Lion: In "Pirates", when Bandit roughly rocks the hammock during the "big storm" part of the pirate game, she gets scared and gets off. Later in the game, she faces her fear and climbs back into the hammock tosave Bluey and Bingo after Bandit (aka the whale) "swallows them whole". Ears as Hair: Her ears are tied up in two hair ties, making it appear she has pigtails. Girlish Pigtails: Her ears are in two hair ties, making it look like she has pigtails, and she is a young girl of about four through five.

characters.name: Lila
characters.description: Best Friend: She is Bingo's best friend and will remain so through to at least graduating university. A Day in the Limelight: She is the central focus on her debut "Daddy Dropoff" and later with Bingo in "Slide". Friend to Bugs: In "Slide", she and Bingo protect bugs from getting squished on the water slide. Shrinking Violet: She was extremely shy when she first joined kindergarten and couldn't make friends. Thankfully, her meeting Bingo helped her overcome this fear.

characters.name: Bentley
characters.description: Always Identical Twins: Averted, as she and Zarahave different fur patterns that make them easier to identify. Character Development: In “Bike”, she has trouble reaching the monkey bars in the park. She succeeds by the end of the episode,but then has trouble getting down. Determinator: In “Bike”, she is determined to reach the monkey bars in the park. Her determination finally pays off towards the end by climbing on one of the monkey bars’ poles. Twin Theme Naming: Averted; her name “Bentley” and her twin sister’s name “Zara” share no common theme.

characters.name: Zara
characters.description: Always Identical Twins: Averted, as she and Bentleyhave different fur patterns that make them easier to identify. All There in the Manual: Her name was revealed in Bentley’s Bluey.tv description. Twin Theme Naming: Averted; her name “Zara” and her twin sister’s name “Bentley” share no common theme.

characters.name: Buddy
characters.description: Cloud Cuckoolander: Downplayed — he often stares into space, and the official website describes him as "a little odd". Furry Reminder:He commonly has his tongue sticking out of his mouth even when it's closed, more or less like real life pugs.In "Bob Bilby", he pants like a real dog before Bingo leaves. He commonly has his tongue sticking out of his mouth even when it's closed, more or less like real life pugs. In "Bob Bilby", he pants like a real dog before Bingo leaves. Nose Nuggets: He's commonly seen picking his nose. In "The Creek" he even wipes the finger he used to pick his nose on the slide he's on.

characters.name: Jasper G.
characters.description: Cheerful Child: He enthusiastically gushes about his new toy and wants to have another game of Pass the Parcel with "Lucky's Dad's Rules". Genki Guy: He behaves enthusiastically and he does karate. Kids Love Dinosaurs: He has a dinosaur sticker on his birthday card, and he's a five-year-old boy.

characters.name: Sadie
characters.description: Ambiguously Related: She's occasionally seen with the baker dog from "Markets", which could imply that she is his daughter, but it's left unstated.

characters.name: Lulu
characters.description: Adorably Precocious Child: Despite clearly being younger than her brother, Lulu is smart enough to call out her brother on not sitting still and to ask in a complete sentence "Why can't you do as you’re told?" as though she herself were a tiny adult. Mouthy Kid: Downplayed, but she sometimes makes imprudent remarks towards her brother and father. Older Than She Looks: Despite being around the same size as Socks and Dusty, who are both around 2 years old, theWhere's Bluey? At Easterbook shows her attending Bingo's kindy, suggesting her to be around 4-5 years old. Species Surname: Her last name Russell is a reference to her beinga Jack Russell Terrier.

characters.name: Digger
characters.description: Big Brother Instinct: He looks out for Rusty and isn't sure about him playing Cricket with the older boys for fear of Rusty getting hurt. Odd Name Out: He is the only one out of his siblings not to have an "-usty" name. Shared Family Quirks: He plays cricket like his little siblings. Squat's in a Name: He's never shown actually digging.

characters.name: Dusty
characters.description: The Baby of the Bunch: She is the youngest in her family, andher older brothers protect and look after her. Big Brother Worship: She looks up to Rusty and admires him as her older brother. Cheerful Child: She is an excitable and energetic little girl. Family Theme Naming: Her name is the combination of her older brothersDigger and Rusty. I Have Brothers: Her two older brothers, Digger and Rusty, teach her how to play cricket.

characters.name: Lila's Brother
characters.description: Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: He wears a bracelet. One-Shot Character: He only appeared in "Pass The Parcel". Small Role, Big Impact: He broke the piñata, resulting in Sheila making Pat in charge of Pass the Parcel so she can clean up the mess, which makes Pat realize the new rules, which is what kickstarted the episode to begin with. Strong Family Resemblance: He bears a lot of resemblance to his big sister and mother. The Troublemaker: He breaks the pinata at his big sister, Lila's party

characters.name: Jean-Luc
characters.description: A French-speaking black Lab from Canada that Bluey befriends while camping. Cheerful Child: He spends most of his time playing, and doesn't seem bothered by the language barrier. Does Not Speak Common: He understands very little English and can't speak it at all, but he and Bluey still get along swimmingly, their language barrier simply being a fun challenge to coordinating their play. Unfortunately, this means he couldn't properly say goodbye to her, breaking her heart. Dub Name Change: In the French dub,not only does he speak English, but is given an English name, Johnny. Freeze-Frame Bonus: Episodes such as "The Show" feature drawings of him and Bluey.

characters.name: Mia
characters.description: Fiery Redhead: Inverted. She has long orange ears but has a calm and gentle demeanor. Friend to All Children: She gets along well with Bluey and loves giving her piggyback rides and writing her letters as shown in "Barky Boats". Nice Girl: She's a sweet and friendly girl. Puppy Love: "Barky Boats" implies that she has a crush on Captain, who is around the same age as her. Twice Shy: In "Barky Boats", it's implied that Mia and Captain both have feelings for each other,but they are too shy to admit it.

characters.name: Captain
characters.description: Friend to All Children: He gets along well with Mackenzie as his buddy and is shown to like playing with him in "Barky Boats". Nice Guy: He is nice and friendly. Puppy Love: "Barky Boats" implies that he has a crush on Mia, who is around the same age as him. Twice Shy: In "Barky Boats", it's implied that Mia and Captain both have feelings for each other,but they are too shy to admit it.

characters.name: Dougie
characters.description: All There in the Manual: He's never actually named onscreen; we only know his name because his mother is credited as "Dougie's Mum". Cheerful Child: He spends most of his time happily playing. Informed Attribute: The official website states that he and Bingo are friends, but they're never shown interacting. The Voiceless:Because he's deaf.

characters.name: Winnie
characters.description: Commonality Connection: She befriends Bluey after realizing how much they have in common, like both having fathers who take them to the park early in the morning and having younger sisters who like to sleep in. Cheerful Child: She is a cheerful and energetic girl. Ms. Imagination: Like Bluey, she’s very imaginative with her games. Nice Girl: She’s very friendly and gets along well with Bluey.

characters.name: Calypso
characters.description: An Australian Shepherd who is Bluey's primary school teacher. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: She wears a blue bandana around her neck. Cool Teacher: A kind and caring teacher to her students, who is always patient with them, and encourages them to do their best. First-Name Basis: Everyone, including the kids, calls her by her first name. Hippie Teacher: Played positively; the kids call her by her first name and her approach to teaching is very laid-back and focused on play, introspection, emotional intelligence, andappreciation for nature. Justified in that she works at a Waldorf/Steiner school, where this kind of teaching method is the entire point.

characters.name: Mrs. Retriever
characters.description: A Golden Retriever who is Bingo's Kindy teacher. Cool Teacher: She is kind and friendly to her students and tries to make learning fun for them. Exhausted Eye Bags: She has small bags under her eyes.This is likely a result of working with younger children as a teacher, which can be a stressful experience at times. Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: A Golden Retriever who is friendly and kindhearted. Last-Name Basis: A downplayed example; so far, she is only addressed as "Mrs. Retriever" with an unknown first name.

characters.name: Frank
characters.description: A Dalmatian and Chloe's dad. All There in the Manual: A Bluey magazine in September 2021 reveals his name as Frank. Bad "Bad Acting": When he first played as the octopus with Chloe in “Octopus”. Good Parents: In “Octopus”, he does his best to play along with the octopus game’s rules despite finding them silly or illogical to make his daughter happy. When Chloe ends the game andcoldly says that Bluey’s dad is more fun than he is, he goes to the computer to learn more facts about octopi so that he can be a better octopus in their game and even teaches his daughter facts about sea creatures. Lack of Imagination: Initially, Frank isn't able to play "Octopus" the same way as Bandit because he's more of a literal thinker. He gets better towards the end, once he and Chloe brainstorm their own way of playing the titular game.

characters.name: Jack's Dad
characters.description: Action Dad: Drove an all-wheel drive vehicle on a four-wheel road to get to his son’s school in "Explorers". No Sense of Direction: Downplayed. In "Explorers", he admits he doesn't remember how to drive to Jack's school because he "puts on Sat Nav and zones out". Once Maynard hands him a map, he manages to get there. Parents as People: While he does love his son, he sometimes has trouble managing Jack's symptoms ofADHD. Species Surname: His last name Russell is a reference to his breed:a Jack Russell Terrier. Unnamed Parent: His first name is yet to be revealed and is simply credited as "Jack's Dad".

characters.name: Bella
characters.description: Canine Confusion: She has naturally pink fur, which is not a color real-life dogs can have. Older Than They Look: She is a mother of nine children, but has no wrinkles, gray hairs, or any other visible signs of aging. Rose-Haired Sweetie: She has pink fur and in “Baby Race”, she gives a heartfelt message to Chilli and reassures her thatshe’s doing a great job as a parent.

characters.name: Fido
characters.description: One of the Kids: Like Bandit, he enjoys playing games with the children. Stock Animal Name: He's a dog named Fido. Sweet Tooth: He's shown enjoying banana bread and sugar packets.

characters.name: Daisy and Marcus
characters.description: Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Both wear glasses, and Marcus wears a bow tie. Brits Love Tea: They're English, and they enjoy drinking tea. Smart People Wear Glasses: Marcus wears glasses and he's a university lecturer. Sweet Tooth: They're commonly seen eating biscuits and cakes.

characters.name: Rusty's Parents
characters.description: Barefoot Cartoon Animal: Rusty's father doesn't wear clothes at home, but when he's in his military uniform, he wears a helmet, shirt, and pants, but no shoes. Good Parents: Whenever Rusty's father is deployed, he writes letters to his children, and he brings them back presents and hangs out with them when he's not drafted. Housewife: Rusty's mother does the cooking, and he implies in "Mums and Dads" that she stays home all day. Shared Family Quirks: Rusty's father plays cricket just like his three kids. Unnamed Parent: Neither of their names are known.

characters.name: Sheila
characters.description: Friend to All Children: She's unhappy when Bingo is made to cry, and she has two children of her own. Nice Girl: She's shown to be compassionate in "Pass the Parcel", where she sheds aSingle Tearout of sympathy for Bingo and she and Chilli give Pat aDeath Glarefor making Bingo cry. Rhyme Theme Naming: She and her daughter's names rhyme. Shared Family Quirks: She and her daughter Lila are both compassionate - Sheila feels sorry for Bingo when she cries in "Pass the Parcel", and Lila is always nice to her best friend Bingo.

characters.name: Indy's Mother
characters.description: Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: She wears earrings, a necklace, and a belt. Ears as Hair: Being an Afghan Hound like her daughter, her ears resemble long hair and she wears earrings under them in a place where a human would. Granola Girl: She's peace-loving, enjoys things such as dreamcatchers and crystals, and has a list of things she dislikes in food (e.g. dairy, gluten, additives). Supreme Chef: She runs a popular baking stand at the market. Sweet Baker: Downplayed; she's an earthy, friendly woman and she bakes, but as a hobby rather than a profession.

characters.name: Snickers's Mother
characters.description: Friend to All Children: She's shown enjoying playing with the kids, and the official website says that she loves watching her friends' kids grow. Nature Lover: Her description on the official website describes her as enjoying sunshine and picnics in the park. Unnamed Parent: Her real name is unknown.

characters.name: Sparky and Chippy
characters.description: Fat and Skinny: Sparky has a wider appearance compared to Chippy's slimmer physique. Good All Along: When they first arrive in "Tradies", Bluey and Bingo declare them enemies and spy on them as they work in their backyard to dig out information. However, when Sparky shares his extra ice cream cone with them as they sit down and talk to him, they find out that he and Chippy aren't such bad guys after all and start warming up to them. In-Series Nickname: Before learning their names, Bluey and Bingo nicknamed Sparky "Big Belt" based on the utility belt he wears and Chippy "Chocolate Milk" based on the beverage he was drinking. Meaningful Name: "Sparky" is Australian slang for an electrician while "Chippy" is Australian slang for a carpenter, both fitting names for tradesmen. Sweet Tooth: As shown in "Tradies":Chippy drinks a bottle of chocolate milk,thus earning the nickname "Chocolate Milk" from Bluey and Bingo when spying on them.Sparky and Chippyboth yell, "Ice cream!" in delight along with Bluey and Bingowhen hearing the ice cream truck arrive and stop to buy an ice cream cone. When Chippy gets distracted from another call with Cherry, Sparky offers the girls his extra cone as they chat, which makes Bluey and Bingo realize thathe's actually a friendly guy once they get to know him.Later, the girls set out a slice of pie for Sparky to eat when they no longer consider him an enemy.

characters.name: Bucky Dunstan
characters.description: A Toy Fox Terrier who is a smooth-talking real estate agent. Blatant Lies: He tells the sheepdog couple that "Queensland summers aren't all that hot" when convincing them tobuy the Heeler house.This is obviously false to anyone who's actually been to Queensland during the summer. Early-Bird Cameo: Bucky was first mentioned and appeared as a sketch drawn by Bandit in "Dragon", with Bandit offhandedly mentioning that he's now a real estate agent. He made his physical debut in "The Sign" and it's revealed that he did indeed become a real estate agent. Half-Dressed Cartoon Animal: He wears a white suit and black tie (which is likely his work uniform) with no pants and is one of the few characters depicted wearing clothes. Innocently Insensitive: In "Dragon", he unintentionally made Bandit give up drawing altogether when they were six by telling him that his car drawings didn't look like cars.

characters.name: Old Pug
characters.description: And There Was Much Rejoicing: The Heelers and Doreen celebrate and praise Muffin for successfully haggling the old pug into trading the Granny Mobile. Barefoot Cartoon Animal: She wears a dress and cardi, but no shoes. Fantastic Racism: Downplayed. The old pug lady tells Chili to “stay out of it” and negatively addresses her as “cattle dog”. Gonk: She is a pug, so she is predictably... not pretty. Grumpy Old Woman: She is old and grouchy to everyone.

characters.name: Cherry
characters.description: Edible Theme Naming: She's named after a fruit. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: She gets very angry with Chippy and they argue and she sulks about driving him to work, but she eventually reconciles with him, and he loves her enough to have a cherry tattoo.

characters.name: Busker
characters.description: Cool Teacher: Implied in the minisode "Alongside" as he's shown giving music lessons to Honey. Everyone Calls Him "Barkeep": Only known as Busker or the Busker, his real name is unknown yet. Everything Is an Instrument: In "Dance Mode", he's out in public playing a "thongaphone", which is a set of plastic piping with sandals. Street Musician: The Busker is seen in "Markets" and "Dance Mode" as one, playing music at public venues.
